article_content: When Susan Knight noticed her baby daughter had an irritation in one of her eyes, she assumed it was due to a pre-existing squint. But when Millie was three, surgeons correcting her eye condition noticed scarring on her right retina. After several trips to Great Ormond Street, Millie was diagnosed with the rare condition known as Toxocariasis—which she had caught after ingesting the eggs of the Roundworm parasite, Toxocara. There are around 50 cases reported each year in the UK, usually in young children. Millie, 13, has been on antibiotics since a parasite infection affected her vision. Undaunted, she now hopes to be part of the Team GB Winter Paralympic Ski team in the future. Toxocara is found in the feces of dogs and cats and can contaminate the soil in gardens, parks, and even playgrounds. If accidentally ingested, the roundworm eggs hatch into larvae that penetrate through the walls of the digestive tract and in rare cases can migrate to the eyes and cause serious sight problems. Millie, who lives near Canterbury and had grown up on a farm, had spent her young life surrounded by animals and picked up the parasite when she was one. However, in her case, the infection had remained dormant for several years and she had displayed no symptoms. Then when Millie was six, the condition reactivated—unusually this time in her left eye. She experienced bouts of feeling poorly, but it wasn't until her teacher noticed a decline in her sight at school that doctors realized what must have happened. Her mother said: 'We looked after all manner of animals when Millie was young, from sheep to household cats and dogs. Millie first contracted the condition at around the age of one, which remained undercover for years until it finally attacked when she was six. During a three-week period, Millie had lost a lot of her sight. We were first referred to an optometrist and then swiftly to Great Ormond St Hospital, as Millie’s vision became worse. Millie ended up having to make weekly visits to Moorfields Eye Hospital, where the infected eye was treated with steroids. She has been on antibiotics ever since.' Millie has scarring in her central vision and is classified as B2 in disability terms—a stage between being blind and visually impaired. Toxocariasis is a rare infection caused by roundworm parasites (Toxocara). It is spread from animals to humans via their infected feces. Ocular larva migrans is the least common but potentially most serious type of toxocariasis. The condition can develop if the roundworm parasites move into the eyes. The main symptoms of ocular larva migrans are blurred or cloudy vision and irritation of the eyes. Left untreated, ocular larva migrans can result in permanent vision loss, although only one eye is usually affected. It affects around 50 people a year and usually affects young children. Treatment involves taking medication to kill the parasites. Most people will quickly make a full recovery and won't experience any long-term complications. Source: NHS. But Millie wouldn't let the condition hold her back. Her mother said: 'She was as cool as a cucumber and has coped so well. I'm very proud of her.' Millie had gone on a skiing holiday in France just before her sight deteriorated and was determined to continue with the sport. 'She really took to it and loved it,' Susan said. 'It is difficult as she can't see much of what she's skiing on and other people. But she never thinks of it as difficult, as she doesn't know any different. She also has headphones so she can talk to me while she's skiing.' Now 13, Millie has just returned from Austria, where she has been training with the Team GB Winter Paralympic Ski team. She hopes to compete in the 2018 games, which will be held in South Korea. The best way to help prevent the rare condition is for dog owners to not only clear up after their pets but to regularly worm them as well. Maggie Fisher from the European Scientific Counsel of Companion Animal Parasites explains: 'The Roundworm (Toxocara) lives in animal feces but can survive even once owners have cleaned up after their pets. In fact, Toxocara is such a resilient parasite it takes bleach and plenty of elbow grease to eradicate it completely. The only way to be sure your pet is not spreading this parasite is to worm regularly—this can be undertaken on a monthly basis to break the life cycle of the parasite.' However, research from the ‘It’s a Jungle Out There’ report from Bayer Animal Health revealed that 75 percent of owners do not regularly worm their pet, while half don't clear up after their dogs. For further advice about preventing pet parasites at www.itsajungle.co.uk.
translated_content: Kun Susan Knight huomasi vauvansa silmän ärsytyksen, hän oletti sen johtuvan jo olemassa olevasta silmänkierrosta. Mutta kun Millie oli kolmen vuoden ikäinen, silmälääkärit huomasivat hänen oikean verkkokalvonsa arpia. Useiden vierailujen jälkeen Great Ormond Streetillä Millielle diagnosoitiin harvinainen tila nimeltä Toxocariasis – jonka hän oli saanut nielaistuaan suolistomadon munia, Toxocaraa. Tapauksia raportoidaan noin 50 vuodessa Isossa-Britanniassa, yleensä pienillä lapsilla. Millie, 13-vuotias, on ollut antibiooteilla siitä lähtien, kun loisinfektio vaikutti hänen näkökykyynsä. Hän toivoo nyt pääsevänsä osaksi Team GB Winter Paralympic Ski -joukkuetta tulevaisuudessa. Toxocara löytyy koirien ja kissojen ulosteista ja voi saastuttaa maaperää puutarhoissa, puistoissa ja jopa leikkikentillä. Jos ne nielaistaan vahingossa, suolistomadon munat kuoriutuvat toukiksi, jotka tunkeutuvat ruoansulatuskanavan seinämien läpi ja harvoin voivat vaeltaa silmiin ja aiheuttaa vakavia näköongelmia. Millie, joka asuu Canterburyn lähellä ja oli kasvanut maatilalla, oli viettänyt lapsuutensa eläinten ympäröimänä ja sai loisinfektiota ollessaan vuoden ikäinen. Tapauksessa infektio oli kuitenkin ollut uinuva useita vuosia eikä hän ollut osoittanut oireita. Sitten kun Millie oli kuusivuotias, tila aktivoitui – tällä kertaa epätavallisesti hänen vasemmassa silmässään. Hän koki ajoittaisia huonovointisuuksia, mutta vasta hänen opettajansa huomasi hänen näkökykynsä heikkenevän koulussa lääkärit ymmärsivät, mitä oli tapahtunut. Hänen äitinsä sanoi: 'Kun Millie oli pieni, me huolehdimme kaikenlaisista eläimistä, lampaita myöten talouden kissoista ja koirista. Millie sai tartunnan noin yhden ikäisenä, joka pysyi piilossa vuosia, kunnes se lopulta iski häneen kuuden ikäisenä. Kolmen viikon aikana Millie menetti paljon näkökykyään. Meidät lähetettiin ensin optometristille ja sitten nopeasti Great Ormond St Hospitaliin, kun Millien näkö heikkeni. Millie päätyi tekemään viikoittaisia vierailuja Moorfields Eye Hospitaliin, missä tartunnan saanut silmä hoidettiin steroidien avulla. Hän on ollut antibiooteilla siitä lähtien.' Milliellä on arpia keskusnäössään ja hänet luokitellaan vammaisuusluokkaan B2 – vaihe, joka on sokeuden ja näkövammaisuuden välillä. Toxocariasis on harvinainen infektio, jonka aiheuttavat suolistomadot (Toxocara). Se leviää eläimistä ihmisiin niiden tartuntaisesta ulosteesta. Ocular larva migrans on vähemmän yleinen, mutta mahdollisesti vakavin toxocariasiksen muoto. Tila voi kehittyä, jos suolistomadot pääsevät silmiin. Ocular larva migransin pääoireet ovat samea tai sumuttava näkö ja silmien ärsytys. Hoitamattomana ocular larva migrans voi johtaa pysyvään näönmenetykseen, vaikka yleensä vain toinen silmä joutuu vaaraan. Se vaikuttaa noin 50 ihmiseen vuodessa ja yleensä pieniin lapsiin. Hoitoon kuuluu lääkkeiden ottaminen loisten tappamiseksi. Useimmat toipuvat nopeasti täydellisesti eivätkä koe pitkäaikaisia komplikaatioita. Lähde: NHS. Mutta Millie ei antanut tilanteen estää itseään. Hänen äitinsä sanoi: 'Hän oli tyyni kuin kurkku ja on selviytynyt niin hyvin. Olen erittäin ylpeä hänestä.' Millie oli ollut laskettelulomalla Ranskassa juuri ennen näkönsä heikentymistä ja oli päättänyt jatkaa urheilua. 'Hän rakastui siihen ja rakasti sitä', Susan sanoi. 'Se on vaikeaa, koska hän ei näe paljoakaan sitä, mitä hiihtää, eikä muita ihmisiä. Mutta hän ei koskaan ajattele sitä vaikeaksi, koska hän ei tiedä mitään muuta. Hänellä on myös kuulokkeet, jotta hän voi puhua minun kanssani hiihdon aikana.' Nyt 13-vuotias Millie on juuri palannut Itävallasta, jossa hän on harjoitellut Team GB Winter Paralympic Ski -joukkueen kanssa. Hän toivoo pääsevänsä kilpailemaan vuoden 2018 kisoissa, jotka järjestetään Etelä-Koreassa. Paras tapa auttaa harvinaisen tilan ehkäisyssä on, että koiranomistajat eivät vain siivoa lemmikkinsä jälkeen, vaan myös madottavat niitä säännöllisesti. Maggie Fisher European Scientific Counsel of Companion Animal Parasitesista selittää: 'Suolistomato (Toxocara) elää eläinten ulosteissa, mutta voi selviytyä edelleen, vaikka omistajat ovat siivonneet lemmikkiensä jälkeen. Todellakin Toxocara on niin kestävä loinen, että sen hävittäminen vaatii valkaista ja runsaasti kyynärpään rasvaa. Ainoa tapa varmistaa, ettei lemmikkinne levitä tätä loista, on madottaa säännöllisesti – tämä voidaan suorittaa kuukausittain katkaisemaan loisen elinkierrosta.' Kuitenkin Bayer Animal Healthin 'It’s a Jungle Out There' -raportin tutkimus paljasti, että 75 prosenttia omistajista ei madota lemmikkiään säännöllisesti, kun taas puolet ei siivoa koiriensa jälkeen. Lisää neuvoja lemmikkiloisten ehkäisyyn osoitteessa www.itsajungle.co.uk.

article_content: Tamara Ecclestone's former partner, Omar Khyami, is facing theft charges after police investigated claims that he stole her jewellery. Khyami, a 40-year-old businessman, is set to appear in court next week, accused of taking valuable items from the wealthy heiress. Their relationship, which lasted two and a half years, ended bitterly in 2012. Khyami was arrested last month. According to Ecclestone, the allegedly stolen jewellery was a gift from her billionaire father, Bernie Ecclestone, the Formula One boss. She reported the matter to the Metropolitan Police after learning that Khyami was trying to sell the jewellery. Khyami, who resides in a flat overlooking London's Hyde Park, attributed the dispute to a misunderstanding. He mentioned being questioned about a 'small piece' of jewellery valued at up to £8,000 but did not specify the item. After his arrest, Khyami stated, 'I don't want to hurt her. It's been two years since we've been together, and I don't know what she wants.' The theft allegations come after a High Court ruling that Ecclestone was wrong to attempt to reclaim a £380,000 Lamborghini she had given to Khyami. She was ordered to pay over £20,000 in compensation to two car companies affected by the case. Ecclestone split from Khyami in 2012 after discovering he had appeared in a sex tape but expressed no regrets about their relationship. In February last year, another ex-boyfriend of hers was sentenced to four years in prison for attempting to blackmail her for £200,000. A Metropolitan Police spokesperson confirmed, 'Police in Kensington and Chelsea have charged Omar Al Khyami, 40, of Bayswater Road, London, with theft in a dwelling. He has been released on bail to appear at West London Magistrates' Court later this month.' It has been reported that the Crown Prosecution Service has decided to drop the theft charge against Khyami.

article_content: Leah Vincent was born into the Yeshivish community, a fundamentalist sect of ultra-Orthodox Judaism, as the fifth of 11 children to a prominent Orthodox rabbi in Pittsburgh. Raised to worship God and the men who ruled their world, Leah and her siblings were prepared for a tradition-bound future. At 15, Leah was readying for marriage, but her life took a drastic turn at 16 when she was caught exchanging letters with a male friend, questioning her faith. This violation of religious law marked her as impure, leading to her eventual expulsion from her family. Leah's parents, fearing her behavior would affect their other children's marriage prospects, sent her to New York City before her 18th birthday. Alone in a studio apartment in Kensington, Brooklyn, Leah struggled to adapt to secular life. Her strict upbringing had taught her to be modest and obedient, abstaining from interactions with unmarried men. This lack of preparation led to a series of risky relationships, including a rape at 17. Leah's journey was marked by loneliness and a search for male approval. She engaged in self-harm, attempted suicide, and briefly worked as a prostitute. Despite these challenges, she found solace in education, excelling at Brooklyn College and later earning a master's degree from Harvard's Kennedy School of Government. Leah eventually found love and stability, marrying Zeke, who also left a Hasidic upbringing. Together, they have a daughter. Leah's story highlights the struggles of breaking free from religious fundamentalism and the broader issues facing young women grappling with sexuality and identity. Her journey from oppression to self-determination is a testament to her resilience and determination.
translated_content: Leah Vincent syntyi Yeshivish-yhteisöön, ultraortodoksisen juutalaisuuden fundamentalistiseen haaraan, viidentenä 11:stä lapsesta tunnetulle ortodoksiselle rabille Pittsburghissä. Kasvatettuna palvomaan Jumalaa ja miesten valtaa heidän maailmassaan, Leah ja hänen sisaruksensa valmistautuivat perinteiden sidottuun tulevaisuuteen. 15-vuotiaana Leah valmistautui avioliittoon, mutta hänen elämänsä kääntyi ratkaisevasti 16-vuotiaana, kun hän jäi kiinni kirjeenvaihdosta miesystävän kanssa, jossa hän kyseenalaisti uskonsa. Tämä uskonnon lain rikkominen merkitsi häntä epäpuhtaaksi, mikä johti lopulta hänen erottamiseensa perheestä. Leahin vanhemmat, pelätessään että hänen käytöksensä vaikuttaisi muiden lasten avioliittomahdollisuuksiin, lähettivät hänet New Yorkiin ennen hänen 18-vuotissyntymäpäiväänsä. Yksin asunnossa Kensingtonissa, Brooklynissä, Leah kamppaili sopeutumisessa sekulaariin elämään. Hänen tiukka kasvatuksensa oli opettanut häntä olemaan vaatimaton ja kuuliainen, pidättäytyen vuorovaikutuksista naimattomien miesten kanssa. Tämä valmistautumattomuus johti riskialttiisiin suhteisiin, mukaan lukien raiskaus 17-vuotiaana. Leahin matka oli merkitsemätön yksinäisyydellä ja miehen hyväksynnän etsimisellä. Hän osallistui itsetuhoon, yritti itsemurhaa ja työskenteli lyhyesti prostituoituna. Näistä haasteista huolimatta hän löysi lohtua koulutuksesta, menestyen Brooklyn Collegessa ja myöhemmin ansaiten maisterin tutkinnon Harvardin Kennedyn valtiotieteellisestä korkeakoulusta. Leah löysi lopulta rakkauden ja vakauden, mennessä naimisiin Zeken kanssa, joka myös jätti hasidilaisen taustansa. Yhdessä heillä on tytär. Leahin tarina korostaa taistelua uskonnollisen fundamentalismin irrottamisesta ja laajemmat ongelmat, joihin nuoret naiset törmäävät koettaessaan sukupuolisuutta ja identiteettiä. Hänen matkansa sortamisesta itsenäiseen päättämisoikeuteen on todiste hänen kestävyydestään ja päättäväisyydestään.

article_content: NEW DELHI: Realty firm Godrej Properties on Thursday reported a 22 percent rise in its consolidated net profit to Rs 66.80 crore and an over two-fold jump in sales bookings to Rs 5,034 crore during the September quarter. Its net profit stood at Rs 54.96 crore in the year-ago period. Total income rose to Rs 605.11 crore during the July-September period of the 2023-24 financial year from Rs 369.20 crore in the corresponding period of the previous year, according to a regulatory filing. In an investors' presentation, Godrej Properties informed that its sales bookings jumped over two-fold to Rs 5,034 crore in the second quarter of this fiscal year compared to Rs 2,409 crore in the year-ago period due to higher volumes. The company said this is its 'highest-ever quarterly sales booking value'. It achieved Rs 2,016 crore in sales bookings from a single project -- Godrej Tropical Isle -- in Noida. Godrej Properties, which is a real estate arm of the business conglomerate Godrej Group, is one of the leading real estate developers in the country. It has projects across various cities but focuses mainly on the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, Delhi-NCR, Pune, and Bengaluru. Pirojsha Godrej, Executive Chairperson of Godrej Properties, said: 'The residential real estate sector in India has been very strong and resilient over the past two years, and we believe the real estate cycle will continue to strengthen over the next few years.' The significant levels of business development the company has executed over the past several years provide it the opportunity to maximize the growth opportunities available in the market, he said. 'Our topmost priority is bringing these projects to market in the upcoming quarters,' Godrej said. 'We saw a strong demand for our new launches this quarter and we are delighted with the response to our project, Godrej Tropical Isle in Noida, which received bookings of more than Rs 2,000 crore within the quarter, making it GPL's most successful ever launch,' he highlighted.

Sen nettotulos oli 54,96 kroonua vuotta aiemmin. Kokonaistulot nousivat 605,11 kroonuun heinä-syyskuun jaksolla vuoden 2023-2024 taloudellisena vuotena 369,20 kroonusta vastaavalla jaksona edellisenä vuonna sääntelyilmoituksen mukaan. Sijoittajien esityksessä Godrej Properties ilmoitti, että sen myyntivaraukset nousivat yli kaksinkertaisesti 5 034 kroonuun tämän taloudellisen vuoden toisella neljänneksellä verrattuna 2 409 kroonuun vuotta aiemmin korkeampien volyymien vuoksi. Yhtiö sanoi, että tämä on sen 'korkein neljänneksen myyntivarauksen arvo koskaan'. Se saavutti 2 016 kroonua myyntivarauksista yhdestä projektista -- Godrej Tropical Isle -- Noidassa. Godrej Properties, joka on liike-elämän konglomeraatti Godrej Groupin kiinteistöhaara, on yksi maan johtavista kiinteistökehittäjistä. Sillä on hankkeita eri kaupungeissa, mutta se keskittyy pääasiassa Mumbain metropolialueelle, Delhi-NCR:lle, Puneen ja Bengaluruun. Pirojsha Godrej, Godrej Propertiesin toimitusjohtaja, sanoi: 'Asuntokiinteistösektori Intiassa on ollut hyvin vahva ja kestävä viimeisten kahden vuoden ajan, ja uskomme, että kiinteistömarkkinoiden kierto jatkaa vahvistumistaan seuraavina vuosina.' Merckittävät liiketoimintakehityksen tasot, jotka yritys on toteuttanut viimeisen vuosien aikana, antavat sille mahdollisuuden hyödyntää markkinoilla tarjolla olevia kasvumahdollisuuksia, hän sanoi. 'Ylin tavoitteemme on tuoda nämä hankkeet markkinoille tulevina neljänneksinä', Godrej sanoi. 'Näimme vahvan kysynnän uusille julkaisuillemme tänä neljänneksenä ja olemme tyytyväisiä vastaukseen projektiimme, Godrej Tropical Isle Noidassa, joka sai yli 2 000 kroonua varauksia neljänneksen aikana tehden siitä GPL:n menestyksekkäimmän koskaan julkaisun', hän korosti.

PUBLISHED: 05:31 EST, 29 May 2012 | UPDATED: 01:22 EST, 30 May 2012 A great-grandmother who suffered a fractured skull after being beaten as she lay in her own bed has died in hospital in the early hours of this morning. Emma Winnall was found unconscious and covered in blood when carers came to check on her in her home in Birmingham earlier this month. The 93-year-old died from complications arising from her injuries at 4:30 am today, West Midlands Police reported. Scroll down for video. Attack: Emma Winnall, pictured in a photograph released by her family as she lay ill in hospital, was assaulted as she slept at her home in Moseley, Birmingham, sometime between 9 pm on April 30 and 9 am the next day. Superintendent Richard Baker, Head of Major Crime at West Midlands Police, stated: 'This is desperately sad news. Our condolences go out to Emma's family and friends. Clearly, this has now become a murder inquiry.' Re-appealing for information about the offense, he added: 'This was a shocking attack on a defenseless, elderly woman as she slept in her own bed. No one capable of carrying out such a despicable attack deserves protection - I'm asking people to look into their consciences and if they have any suspicions about who may be responsible to contact the police.' Mrs. Winnall had a fractured skull, a broken arm and wrist, and a partially severed finger. The beating was so severe that the frail widow's palms were bruised from her attempts to protect herself, while blood had splattered onto the walls behind her bed. A woman, 56, and a man, 28, were arrested at their home in the Hall Green area of Birmingham on May 17 on suspicion of assault. They were later released on bail until July. The arrests came after a £5,000 reward was offered for information leading to a conviction in the case. Crimestoppers offered the cash reward in a move backed by West Midlands Police. Detective Chief Inspector Sarb Johal said at the time: 'I would like to thank Crimestoppers for offering this reward and say again that local people hold the key to finding who is responsible for this terrible attack. No one capable of carrying out such a despicable attack deserves protection. I’m asking people to look into their consciences and if they have any suspicions about who may be responsible to contact the police.' A shocking picture released by her family in the days after the attack showed the full extent of the appalling injuries Mrs. Winnall suffered to her face. As her family appealed for help in finding her attacker, they revealed that Mrs. Winnall had started to describe the awful moment she was assaulted. Her daughter said she spoke of screaming for help in vain, while the palms of her hands are bruised from her attempts to protect herself. The beating was so severe blood had splattered onto the walls behind her bed. Mrs. Blencoe and her brother John Winnall make their public appeal for information. Detective Chief Inspector Sarb Johal (left) described the level of violence as 'shocking'. Mrs. Winnall’s daughter Joyce Blencoe, 56, spoke last week from West Midlands Police headquarters with her brother John. She said: 'To see your mum viciously beaten and covered in blood has been the most horrific nightmare. It’s broken my heart to hear my frail and defenseless mum manage to say she was screaming for help and no one came.' Mrs. Winnall, who lived in Moseley, Birmingham, worked at the city’s small arms factory during the Second World War. She relied on a wheelchair to get around and lived alone since her husband Frank died in 2006, aged 91. She is survived by five children, seven grandchildren, and four great-grandchildren. article_content: By Alasdair Glennie. The BBC licence fee is 'too high' and should be decriminalised, its former chairman has admitted. Michael Grade, who left the corporation in 2006 to lead ITV, said he feels 'squeamish' about the fact viewers can be sent to prison for not paying the £145.50 charge. Although he supports the principle of charging all households to watch live TV, he called for it to be reduced when it comes up for renewal in 2016. Former BBC chairman Michael Grade believes non-payment of the licence fee should be decriminalised. Lord Grade told a Royal Television Society debate: 'I support the licence fee, but I think it is too high. That is a whole other debate, but nevertheless I fully support the licence fee for the next charter period.' He added: 'I think the big debate is going to be about the issues of criminality, compulsion and so on. I think we all feel a bit squeamish about the fact you can go to prison if you don't pay the fine for not paying the licence fee. If there is a way to decriminalise non-payment of the licence fee, that would be a good thing.' Lord Grade first joined the BBC as controller of BBC1 in 1984, and became its director of programming in 1986. During his time in charge of TV output, he courted controversy by cancelling production of Doctor Who, which he branded 'awful' and 'outdated'. Lord Grade said the BBC must still be allowed to impose penalties on those who fail to pay the licence fee, otherwise it would open the doors to pre-determined programming. After a stint at Channel 4, he became BBC Chairman for two years and now sits as a Conservative peer in the House of Lords. Although he called for licence fee evasion to be decriminalised, Lord Grade said the BBC must still be allowed to impose penalties on those who fail to pay. He said: 'You have to retain compulsion, otherwise you are opening the way for subscription. Subscription means pre-determined, well-known programming that will be guaranteed to drive subscription. You won't get Happy Valley. You will be getting whatever they can pick up in the free-market in competition with Sky.' The Government is currently conducting a year-long review into whether to decriminalise the licence fee. Lord Grade added: 'If you were inventing the United Kingdom today I think there are three institutions you wouldn't create in a modern world. I don't think you would create a hereditary monarchy, I don't think you would create an unelected second chamber, and I don't think you would create an organisation like the BBC and organise for it to have £4 billion of public funding in an age of media plenty, expansion and so on.' 'But you have to believe that there is something in these three institutions that connects with the British public, and the BBC is one of those institutions that relies for its existence not on political whim, not on political dogma, but on the affection and support of the British public.' 'It faces an incredibly difficult few years coming up, not least with the whole argument about how it should be funded.' The Government is currently conducting a year-long review into whether to decriminalise the licence fee. It followed a campaign by backbench MPs to scrap the threat of prison sentences for fee evaders. In 2012, 193,049 people were prosecuted for not paying their TV licence, accounting for one in nine of all magistrates court cases. Most of those found guilty were landed with penalties of up to £1,000 and a criminal record, and between 50 and 70 viewers are sent to jail each year after they fail to pay the court fines.

Michael Grade, joka jätti yhtiön vuonna 2006 johtamaan ITV:tä, sanoi tuntemansa epämukavuutta siitä, että katsojat voivat joutua vankilaan, jos he eivät maksa 145,50 punnan maksua. Entinen BBC:n johtaja Michael Grade uskoo, ettei lisenssimaksun maksamatta jättämistä pitäisi kriminalisoida. Lord Grade sanoi Royal Television Society -keskustelussa: 'Tuen lisenssimaksua, mutta luulen sen olevan liian korkea. Se on kokonaan toinen keskustelu, mutta kuitenkin tuen lisenssimaksua seuraavalle sopimuskaudelle.' Hän lisäsi: 'Suuri keskustelu käydään rikollisuuden, pakottamisen ja niin edelleen aiheista. Kaikki meistä tuntemme hieman epämukavuutta siitä, että voit joutua vankilaan, jos et maksa sakkoa lisenssimaksun maksamatta jättämisestä. Jos on tapa kriminalisoida lisenssimaksun maksamatta jättäminen, se olisi hyvä asia.' Lord Grade liittyi BBC:hen ensimmäisen kerran BBC1:n ohjelmapäällikkönä vuonna 1984 ja tuli sen ohjelmistojen johtajaksi vuonna 1986. Hänen aikanaan ohjelmistojen johdossa hän herätti kohua lopettamalla Doctor Who -tuotannon, jonka hän leimasi 'kauheaksi' ja 'vanhanaikaiseksi'. Lord Grade sanoi, että BBC:n tulee edelleen sallia rangaistukset niille, jotka eivät maksa lisenssimaksua, muuten se avaa ovet ennalta määrättyyn ohjelmistoon. Channel 4:n kautensa jälkeen hänestä tuli BBC:n puheenjohtaja kahdeksi vuodeksi ja nyt hän istuu konservatiivipuolueen edustajana ylähuoneessa. Vaikka hän vaati lisenssimaksun vältelyn kriminalisointia, Lord Grade sanoi, että BBC:n tulee edelleen sallia rangaistukset niille, jotka eivät maksa sitä. Hän sanoi: 'Sinun täytyy säilyttää pakottaminen, muuten avaat tien tilaukseen. Tilaus tarkoittaa ennalta määrättyä, tunnettua ohjelmistoa, joka takaa tilauksen. Et saa Happy Valleyta. Saat mitä tahansa he voivat kerätä vapaasta markkinasta kilpaillen Skyn kanssa.' Hallitus suorittaa tällä hetkellä vuoden mittaisen tarkistuksen siitä, pitäisikö lisenssimaksua kriminalisoida. Lord Grade lisäsi: 'Jos luot uudelleen Yhdistyneet kuningaskunnat tänä päivänä, luulen, että on kolme instituutiota, jotka et luo nykymaailmassa. En luulisi, että luot perinnöllisen monarkian, en luulisi, että luot valitsemattoman toisen kamarin, enkä luulisi, että luot organisaatiota kuten BBC ja järjestäisit sen saamaan 4 miljardia puntaa julkista rahoitusta mediamäärän, laajentumisen ja niin edelleen aikakaudella.' 'Mutta sinun täytyy uskoa, että nämä kolme instituutiota ovat jotain, mikä yhdistää brittiläisen yleisön, ja BBC on yksi niistä instituutioista, joka luottaa olemassaolonsa ei poliittiseen oikkuun, ei poliittiseen dogmiin, vaan brittiläisen yleisön kiintymykseen ja tukeen.' 'Sillä on edessään hyvin vaikeat vuodet, ei vähiten koko keskustelun kanssa siitä, miten sen pitäisi rahoittaa.' Hallitus suorittaa tällä hetkellä vuoden mittaisen tarkistuksen siitä, pitäisikö lisenssimaksua kriminalisoida. Se seurasi takapenkkiryhmän kansanedustajien kampanjaa poistaa vankilatuomiot lisenssimaksun vältelijöiltä. Vuonna 2012 193 049 ihmistä tuomittiin oikeudessa lisenssimaksun maksamatta jättämisestä, mikä vastaa yhdeksäsosaa kaikista tuomioistuinjutuista. Useimmat syyllisiksi todistetuista joutuivat 1 000 punnan sakkoihin ja rikostutkintaan, ja 50–70 katsojaa viedään vankilaan vuosittain, kun he eivät maksa tuomioistuimen sakkoja.

article_content: By Sarah Harris. PUBLISHED: 19:23 EST, 29 May 2013. UPDATED: 02:44 EST, 30 May 2013. Grandparents are a lifeline for busy parents, caring for 1.6 million children and saving families £7.3 billion annually, according to recent research by Grandparents Plus and Age UK. The older generation is increasingly taking on childcare responsibilities, with the total hours dedicated to this role rising from 1.3 billion to 1.7 billion—a 35% increase. This significant contribution, valued at £7.3 billion, has grown from £3.9 billion in 2004. The study analyzed data from Understanding Society, a UK longitudinal survey involving over 11,000 children. Caroline Abrahams from Age UK highlighted the crucial role grandparents play in children's lives, providing affordable childcare that allows parents to continue working. Sam Smethers, CEO of Grandparents Plus, emphasized the need for government support to help grandparents balance work and caring responsibilities. He noted that grandparents are vital in helping families cope with financial pressures and rising childcare costs. On average, grandparents providing childcare dedicate about 20 hours per week, resulting in an annual saving of over £8,600 for a family with two young children. Younger grandmothers, aged 50 to 64, are the most likely to provide care, enabling parents, especially mothers, to work. The report calls for policy changes to recognize the essential role of grandparents in childcare and to support their work-life balance. Legislation should clarify grandparents' rights to take emergency leave for childcare. The planned extension of flexible working rights could benefit both grandparents and mothers in the workforce. Employers, particularly in the public sector, should lead by example in supporting these requests. Smethers warned of a potential childcare gap if grandmothers remain in the workforce longer, impacting mothers' ability to stay employed.

article_content: Simon Cowell praised Lettice for her talent and personality. Quirky yet captivating, Britain's Got Talent continues to showcase the nation's eccentric side. After weeks of magical performances and dynamic dance groups, the contestant pool has been narrowed down to the final 45. Who will claim the £250,000 prize and perform at the Royal Variety Performance? Weekend introduces six hopefuls still in the running... THE HIPPY VIOLINIST: It's clear why the energetic Lettice Rowbotham, 24, struggled in an orchestra. 'People think I'm drunk even when I'm sober,' she laughs. She won a standing ovation from the judges when Simon Cowell told her, 'You're not only brilliant but have a fantastic personality.' Lettice says the encouragement from BGT has driven her forward. 'If I make it to the final, I'm going to play my own stuff and really surprise people,' she shares. Surrey-born Lettice demanded a violin at age four and composed her first tune in a day. She won a scholarship to the prestigious Purcell School of Music but left after a year. 'Musicians are very competitive, while I just want to play because I love it,' she explains. She moved to Greece to teach windsurfing and spent winters in Switzerland, playing her violin on a nightclub roof. 'I'm worried about the environment, so I'd like to plant a tree for every gig I do,' she says. 'And I'd love to encourage kids to leave their laptops and pick up an instrument!' THE GYRATING GRANNY: Dancer Paddy Jones, 79, says her life has been a whirlwind since her electrifying audition. Initially buzzed by Simon, her jaw-dropping performance with partner Nico changed his mind. Amanda adored her so much she pressed the golden buzzer. 'It's been manic ever since,' says Paddy. 'I could do with putting a bag over my head because so many people are asking for my autograph.' Paddy was a professional dancer until age 22 but gave it up to have a family. She started again a decade ago after her husband David died. Nico ran the local dance school, and they began performing together, winning a Spanish TV talent show. Now, Paddy dreams of performing at the Royal Variety, especially if the Queen attends. 'I would die happy knowing I'd done that,' she smiles. THE VENTRILOQUIST WITH TOURETTE'S: Sam Jones, 21, admits ventriloquism is an odd career choice, but it's the only thing that makes him happy. Sam, from Seaford, has suffered from Tourette's syndrome all his life. He taught himself ventriloquism from a library book at age six. His favorite puppet, Baby Leo, has become a crowd pleaser. Sam hopes to raise awareness about Tourette's. 'I was bullied at school, but I've learned to be proud of my condition,' he says. 'A lot of people with Tourette's control it with creativity; mine has been through the puppets.' THE GLAMOUR GIRL GROUP: Girlie trio REAformed—Alexis Economou, Renetta Eagle, and Ebony Cantwell—told judge Alesha Dixon she was their inspiration. Alesha pressed the golden buzzer, sending them straight to the semi-finals. Despite past mistakes, they're determined to succeed. 'We've been practising like mad,' says Renetta. 'This is important for us; we want to be the next Destiny's Child.' THE BLUE-SKINNED DIVA: Fuzzy, pink-haired New Yorker Patsy May, 34, describes her style as influenced by the Muppets. Simon was impressed with her audition, suggesting she could be a future judge. Patsy hopes she's not just a 'token blue' and dreams of marrying into fame and fortune. 'My favorite type of men are celebrities with money,' she trills. THE PINT-SIZED CROONER: Cute-as-a-cupcake James Smith, 15, from Upminster, earned a standing ovation with his rendition of Nina Simone's 'Feeling Good.' 'I believe I've got the potential to win it... maybe,' he says. Despite his success, his parents keep him grounded. 'If the music doesn't work out, I need to be prepared to work in a bank or something boring,' he shrugs.
